papers.title: Enhanced Osseointegration of a Modified Titanium Implant with Bound Phospho-Threonine: A Preliminary In Vivo Study.
papers.abstract: Implant surface topography is a key factor in achieving osseointegration. l-Threonine can be chemically and stably bonded to titanium surfaces by phosphorylation. This study investigated the degree of in vivo osseointegration of an implant with a novel o-phospho-l-threonine (p-Thr)-binding surface. MC3T3-E1 cells were seeded on the p-Thr binding surface and machined surface disks, and initial cell attachment was evaluated. p-Thr-binding and machined surface implants were tested in vivo by implantation into the femurs of three male New Zealand white rabbits, and the osseointegration was assessed by measurement of removal torque (RT) and bone-implant contact (BIC) ratio. Initial cell attachment was greater for the p-Thr-binding than for the machined surface implant group (P < 0.05). In addition, RT and BIC values were higher for the p-Thr-binding surface than for the machined surface (P < 0.05). These results indicate that our implant with a p-Thr-binding surface can achieve enhanced osseointegration.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及钛植入体表面改性以促进骨整合，但未涉及多孔结构、LPBF制造或疲劳测试。
llm.why_not_core: No LPBF fabrication, no porous structure, no mechanical testing (static or fatigue), no stress shielding analysis.

summary_zh.motivation: 通过表面化学改性增强钛植入体的骨整合效果。
summary_zh.method: 将磷酸化苏氨酸结合到钛表面，并进行细胞和动物实验。
summary_zh.result: 改性表面提高了细胞附着、拔出力矩和骨-植入体接触率。
summary_zh.validation: 兔股骨植入实验验证骨整合效果。

summary_en.motivation: To improve osseointegration of titanium implants via chemical surface modification with phospho-threonine.
summary_en.method: Phospho-threonine was covalently bonded to titanium surfaces; in vitro cell attachment and in vivo rabbit femur implantation were performed.
summary_en.result: The modified surface significantly enhanced initial cell attachment, removal torque, and bone-implant contact ratio compared to machined surfaces.
summary_en.validation: In vivo rabbit femur model with removal torque and histomorphometric analysis.
